metadata.titleTag: Extension Cleanup Review for Small Business Books | Balance Beam
metadata.metaDescription: Filed a tax extension because your books were not ready? Balance Beam helps Schedule C filers, partnerships, and S Corps clean up books before extended filing deadlines.
metadata.audience: Schedule C filers, single-member LLC owners, partnerships, and S corporations whose tax returns were extended because their books were not ready
metadata.coreMessage: An extension gives you more time to file. It does not clean up the books.

voice.avoid: hype, fear-based IRS language, tax hacks, loopholes, refund promises

usageNotes.note: Aim for a calm, professional financial-services look. Avoid visual patterns associated with cheap lead-gen funnels: aggressive gradients, neon accents, urgency timers, exclamation-heavy buttons.
Teal (#0F5F5C) is reserved for primary calls to action and primary interactive states. Do not use teal for decorative elements.
Copper (#B87333) is reserved for deadline accents. Do not use copper as a general accent, button color, or for non-deadline UI.
Maintain WCAG AA contrast at minimum for all text and interactive elements. Verify Primary Text on Background and Surface, Muted Text on Background, and CTA label color on Primary CTA.
Never use color alone to convey meaning. Pair color with an icon, label, or text cue (e.g., deadline cards should include the date as text, not only a colored highlight).
Helper and fine-print text must not drop below 14px. Body copy should default to 18px for readability.

section.headline: Filed an extension because your books were not ready?
section.subheadline: An extension gives you more time to file. It does not clean up the books. Balance Beam helps small-business owners review, organize, and clean up the bookkeeping issues that delay tax preparation.
section.aboveTheFoldHook: If your 2025 tax return was extended because the books were behind, unreconciled, or unclear, the deadline is still coming. The right next step is not to wait until September or October. It is to find out what needs to be fixed before the return can be prepared.
section.trustLine: For Schedule C filers, single-member LLCs, partnerships, S corporations, and small-business owners who need tax-ready books before filing.

section.headline: The extension solved the filing deadline. It did not solve the bookkeeping problem.

body.paragraph: Many small-business owners file extensions because the tax return cannot be prepared from the information available in March or April. The issue is often not the tax form itself. The issue is that the books are behind, accounts are not reconciled, transactions are unclear, or the reports cannot be trusted yet.
That is fixable, but it needs a process. Waiting until the extended deadline gets closer usually creates the same problem again, only with less time to clean it up.

section.callout: If the books were not ready by the original deadline, they need attention before the extended deadline.

section.headline: Know the deadline you are working toward.
section.intro: Different business types have different extended federal filing deadlines. Your entity type matters, and cleanup should start early enough to leave time for tax preparation after the books are ready.

card.entityType: Schedule C filers and single-member LLCs
card.description: If you report business income on Schedule C with your individual Form 1040 and filed a valid extension, your extended federal filing deadline is generally October 15, 2026.

card.entityType: Partnerships and multi-member LLCs taxed as partnerships
card.description: If your calendar-year partnership filed an extension for Form 1065, your extended federal filing deadline is generally September 15, 2026.
If your calendar-year S corporation filed an extension for Form 1120-S, your extended federal filing deadline is generally September 15, 2026.

section.caution: An extension is generally an extension of time to file, not an extension of time to pay. C corporation deadlines may differ depending on fiscal year and entity-specific facts. If you are unsure what applies to your situation, talk with your tax professional.

section.headline: What Balance Beam looks at
section.body: The review is designed to identify the bookkeeping issues that may prevent your tax return from being prepared accurately and efficiently. It is not a shortcut around cleanup. It is the first step in understanding what cleanup is actually required.

checklist.item: Bank and credit card reconciliation status
Owner draws, distributions, transfers, and reimbursements
Personal expenses paid from business accounts
Payroll or contractor payment issues that affect the books
Year-end reports needed for tax preparation
Whether prior months need catch-up bookkeeping

objection.question: I already filed an extension, so I have time.
objection.answer: You have more time to file, but the books still need to be reviewed and cleaned up before the return can be prepared. The longer cleanup waits, the less time remains for tax preparation.

objection.question: I just need someone to do my taxes.
objection.answer: If the books are clean, tax preparation may be straightforward. If the books are not ready, the tax return depends on cleanup first. Balance Beam can help determine which situation you are in.

objection.question: My books are in QuickBooks, so they should be fine.
objection.answer: QuickBooks is a tool. The file still needs reconciled accounts, accurate categories, and properly handled owner transactions. A report from QuickBooks is only useful if the activity behind it has been reviewed.

objection.question: I do not know how far behind I am.
objection.answer: That is exactly why the review exists. The first step is identifying what months, accounts, and records need attention.

objection.question: Can you just give me a monthly bookkeeping price?
objection.answer: Monthly bookkeeping pricing depends on whether the books are current or need cleanup first. If prior activity is unreliable, cleanup should be scoped separately before monthly service begins.

item.question: Does filing an extension mean I have more time to pay?
item.answer: Generally, no. An extension gives more time to file the return, not more time to pay tax that was due by the original deadline. If you are unsure whether you paid enough with your extension, talk with your tax professional.

item.question: What if I do not know whether I am a Schedule C filer, partnership, or S corporation?
item.answer: That is common. The intake form includes an "I'm not sure" option. We can help identify the filing path based on your business structure and prior-year return, but formal advice requires an engagement.

item.question: Can you prepare the tax return too?
item.answer: Balance Beam provides tax preparation and bookkeeping services. If your books need cleanup before the return can be prepared, we will separate the cleanup scope from the tax preparation scope so the work is clear.

item.question: What if my tax preparer already filed the extension?
item.answer: That is fine. The review focuses on the bookkeeping issues that may still need to be resolved before the return can be prepared. If another preparer is filing the return, the goal may be to provide cleaner reports and records for that preparer.

item.question: What if I use QuickBooks?
item.answer: QuickBooks helps organize the records, but it does not guarantee the books are accurate. Accounts still need to be reconciled, transactions reviewed, and owner activity handled correctly.

item.question: Do I need cleanup or monthly bookkeeping?
item.answer: It depends on whether the books are current and reliable. If prior activity is incomplete or inaccurate, cleanup usually comes first. Monthly bookkeeping can begin after the file is stable.

item.question: How fast can cleanup be completed?
item.answer: Timing depends on the number of months, accounts, missing records, and complexity of the business. The review helps determine the likely scope and next steps.

item.question: Is this only for California businesses?
item.answer: Balance Beam is based in California and works heavily with California small-business compliance, but the review may be relevant to business owners outside California as well. State-specific requirements should be confirmed during the consultation.

item.question: Is this tax advice?
item.answer: This page is general information, not advice for your specific situation. If you want to talk through how this applies to your business, reach out.

note.description: Deadlines stated on this page reflect calendar-year filers under typical federal rules. C corporation deadlines may differ depending on fiscal year and entity-specific facts. Confirm specifics with a tax professional before relying on dates.
